steps.title: Look before you label
steps.body: Study the strip. Describe the rate and rhythm first, then look closely at each wave.

image.alt: Lead II rhythm strip, regular rhythm, with tall, narrow, peaked T waves
image.caption: Sample strip (illustrative drawing)

steps.prompt: Which electrolyte abnormality best explains these T waves?

image.alt: Lead II rhythm strip, regular rhythm, with tall, narrow, peaked T waves

steps.explanation: Tall, narrow, peaked T waves are an early ECG sign of hyperkalaemia. Check the potassium urgently and treat according to local protocol.
